 :JUDGMENT:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 10,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
SCCH 15 3 MVC No.4393/2020 That on 24.04.2017 at about 3.10 p.m., when the Petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in the TVS XL Moped bearing Reg.No.KA06R0945 and when they reached near Hindiskere gate, NH206 road, Tiptur rural, Tumkur, at that time one Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA44Q5084 ridden by its rider came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to the said accident, rider and Petitioner were thrown out from the vehicle and she had sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Tiptur Government General hospital and after first aid she was shifted to Tiptur Government hospital, wherein she was admitted as an inpatient.

The Petitioner had spent more than Rs.80,000/ towards medical expenses, conveyance,
nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
4.
Prior to the date of the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and she was a Student.
The accident has occurred SCCH 15 4 MVC No.4393/2020 due to the rash and negligent riding of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA44Q5084 by its rider.
The Respondent No.1 is the R.C. owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA44Q 5084.
Therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 had appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its Written statement to the main Petition.

The Respondent No.2 in its Written statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Further it contended that, SCCH 15 5 MVC No.4393/2020
the rider of the offending motorcycle was not holding valid driving license to ride the motorcycle at the time of the accident.

Further it contended that the accident is caused due to the negligence and carelessness of the rider of the TVS Moped bearing Reg.No.KA06R0945 without following traffic rules and regulations and lost the control over the motorcycle and fell down on the road and due to which the Petitioner had sustained injuries.

Further it contended that the Petitioner Reshma vs Jithan M on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114800648/
2 by colluding with Police has lodged false Complaint against the insured vehicle in order to get compensation illegally.

sentences.text: Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
6. On the rival Pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of SCCH 15 6 MVC No.4393/2020 riding of Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA44 Q5084 and as a result, she sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner proves the age and earnings of the Petitioner as stated in the petition?
3. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What Order or Award?

7. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 13 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and has examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 3 documents at Ex.P14 to 16 and closed her side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondent No. 2 did not choose to lead any evidence.

8. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsels for both sides and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
SCCH 15 7 MVC No.4393/2020 Issue No.1 : Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order, for the following :
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioner that, she had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA44Q5084 by its rider.
10. On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA44Q5084 by its rider.

Reshma vs Jithan M on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114800648/
3 11.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, she got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 13 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and she has reiterated the Petition averments in her Chief affidavit.

Ex.P.1 to 9 are the FIR, Complaint, Spot SCCH 15 8 MVC No.4393/2020 mahazar,
Statements, Wound certificate, IMV report and Charge sheet.
Ex.P.10 to Ex.
P.13 are the Outpatient record, Medical bills, Prescriptions and Aadhaar card.

12. Upon going through the documents exhibited, Ex.P.1 and 2 are the True copies of the FIR and Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by the brother of the Petitioner by name Shakeel, the Tiptur rural Police have registered the case against the riders of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA44Q5084 and KA06R0945 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P3 is the Spot mahazar which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P4 to 6 are the Statements of the Petitioner and witnesses.
Ex.P.7 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner had sustained grievous injury.
ExP8 is the IMV report which shows that the said accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.

Ex.P9 is the SCCH 15 9 MVC No.4393/2020 Certified copy of the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Tiptur rural Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA44Q5084 for the offences punishable under Sec.
279 and 338 of IPC.
13.
P.W.1 has been crossexamined by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2.
In the cross examination, PW.1 admitted that there is a head in collusion between their motorcycle and the offending motorcycle.
Further, she admitted that as per IMV Report i.e., Ex.P8 the front portion of both vehicles got damaged.

Admittedly, the IMV Report i.e., Ex.P8 clearly shows the damages found on the front portion of both vehicles which supports the contention of the Respondent about head on collusion between both vehicles.
It is important to note here that at the time of lodging Complaint, the brother of the Petitioner has stated the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the both vehicles.
But, subsequently, the Petitioner and the SCCH 15 10 MVC No.4393/2020 rider of the TVS XL had given further statement about the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle only.
But, upon going through the Spot Mahazar i.e., Ex.P3 clearly shows the accident occurred in the middle of the road.

Moreover, PW.1 admitted that there is head on collusion between both vehicles and IMV report shows the damages found on the front portion of the vehicles which clearly shows there is a some extent of contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the TVS XL bearing Reg.No.KA06R0945 also.

Under such circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the accident had occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the both motorcycles i.e.,
the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA44Q5084 and TVS XL bearing Reg.No.KA06R0945 and due to the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 "Partly in the Affirmative'.
Issue No. 2 and 3:
Both these issues are taken together for common discussion as they are inter linked with each other and to avoid the repetition of facts.

Reshma vs Jithan M on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114800648/
4

As this Tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle and TVS XL, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
15.
It is stated in the petition that, the Petitioner is aged 18 years at the time of accident.
The Petitioner has produced the Aadhar card at Ex.P13 which shows her date of birth was 04.08.2004.
The accident has taken place on 24.04.2017.
Hence, at the time of accident, the Petitioner was aged about 14 years.
16. It is established that the Petitioner had suffered from injury in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
The SCCH 15 12 MVC No.4393/2020 Petitioner has contended that she had sustained grievous injury and she has spent Rs.80,000/ for her medical treatment and other incidental charges.
The Petitioner has produced Wound Certificate at Ex.P7 issued by the Government Hospital, Tiptur, wherein it clearly mentioned that the Petitioner had sustained injury to left arm.
The Doctor has opined that the said injury is grievous in nature.
17. The Petitioner did not choose to examine the doctor who has issued the Wound Certificate as per Ex.P7.
The Petitioner has produced the Medical bills to prove expenditure towards medicines.
The bills at Ex.P11 would reveal that the Petitioner had spent Rs.80,609/ towards medicines.

18. However, PW.1 has not examined any doctor and in the absence of physical disability and considering the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the medical expenses incurred for the treatment and other expenses, this Tribunal is SCCH 15 13 MVC No.4393/2020 of the opinion that awarding global compensation of Rs.1,10,000/ would be just and proper.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.1,10,000/ with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realisation.

19. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA44Q5084 and the rider of the TVS XL bearing Reg.No.KA06R0945.

As per the detailed discussion made in Issue No.1, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA44 Q5084 attributes 75% of contributory negligence and the rider of the TVS XL bearing Reg.No.KA06R0945 attributes 25% of the contributory negligence towards the said accident.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the Owner and Respondent No.2 is SCCH 15 14 MVC No.4393/2020 the Insurer of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA44 Q5084.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.

Therefore,
the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy 75% of the the award amount out of the total award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay 75% of the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 and 3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
20. Issue No.4:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 to 3 , I proceed to pass the following:

5 ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner is entitled for Global Compensation of Rs.1,10,000/ along with SCCH 15 15 MVC No.4393/2020 interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 jointly and  severally liable to pay 75% of the  compensation amount out of the total compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the Offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the Award.

On deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, since the amount is meager, the entire amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of Epayment after her proper identification.

The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
